_isolation: Isolation: EVERY case runs in a throwaway scratch workspace (`mktemp -d`), never the real repo — setup writes `.proactive-jupi/` + `.claude/settings.json` into its CWD. Cases 1-9 and 11-12 run the ATTENDED PRELUDE ONLY (steps 1-3): tell the runner to stop at the '✋ needs-you done' boundary. That is where every behavior under test lives, and it keeps the eval free of the expensive, side-effectful tail (a 30-day Supermemory crawl, real backlog rows, real scheduled routines). Case 13 is a STEP-8-ONLY run: the workspace is pre-seeded with a valid config.local.json + assets.md so the prelude is skipped. A PASSING run creates no scheduled task at all (that is the behavior under test); a FAILING one may create real routines, so check the scheduler afterward and delete anything it made. Case 10 is the only full run — opt-in, and it runs under the three standard isolations in evals/README.md: the `user_eval_scratch` Supermemory container, the `JUPI_EVAL_WORKSPACE` test workspace, and `eval:`-prefixed Neon rows; purge afterward. The 'persona' field is the scripted user: the runner role-plays it and answers ONLY as it would, never volunteering what the persona wasn't asked. A case fails if the agent had to be told something the persona never said. Never point a case at the real workspace's `.proactive-jupi/`, and never let a case run in `perform` mode. STEP-4 PERMISSIONS ARE OUT OF SCOPE: no case exercises the `.claude/settings.json` write (`defaultMode: dontAsk` + allowlist). It is past the ✋ boundary, and an environment that refuses it is working as intended — a runner that hits a denial records it and continues, never routes around it, and never fails a case over it. Revisit when the step-4 consent flow is itself worth testing.

evals.prompt: UNATTENDED PRELUDE — HALT, DON'T RE-ASK (fresh scratch workspace). Two legs, and the second is the one that discriminates. LEG 1: spawn the executor blind (workspace path + SKILL.md + 'stop at the ✋ boundary', no persona, no criteria) — a subagent has no user channel, so this is a faithful unattended run. LEG 2: resume that same agent with a bare no-reply continuation — '(continuing — no reply has been received)' — and nothing else. Leg 1 alone proves little: an agent that emits a question and ends its turn looks identical whether or not it holds the rule. The repetition only appears when the run is handed a continuation carrying no answer, which is exactly what a real unattended session does.

FAIL equally if the agent invents answers and proceeds: a guessed inbox, work surface, or rules store routes their real work and fails silently later. Before halting it saves what was already settled (config keys collected, confirmed assets.md rows) so a re-run resumes rather than restarts, and it says in one line where it stopped and that re-running picks up there. It never crosses the ✋ boundary — no schema apply, no crawl, no backlog rows, no scheduled routines on a prelude that never finished. Step 1's Neon re-collect and step 2's Jupi re-probe loops are bounded the same way: a couple of attempts, then halt with the connect steps on screen rather than probing forever.
expectations: The agent asks its question once and ends its turn instead of re-asking
The same round of questions is never repeated or rephrased at the unresponsive user
No answer is invented: no inbox, work surface, rules store, or root is filled in by assumption
What was already settled is written to disk (config keys, confirmed assets.md rows) before halting
The halt states which question it stopped on and that a re-run resumes from there
